questions.prompt: Which type of reaction is this? “Iron is heated with sulphur to make iron sulphide.”
questions.explanation: Two elements combine into one new substance (Fe + S → FeS).

questions.prompt: Which type of reaction is this? “Magnesium burns in oxygen to make magnesium oxide.”
questions.explanation: Two substances combine into one (2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO).

questions.prompt: Which type of reaction is this? “Copper is burnt in oxygen to make copper oxide.”
questions.explanation: Copper and oxygen combine into one compound (2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO).

questions.prompt: Which type of reaction is this? “Copper carbonate is heated into copper oxide and carbon dioxide.”
questions.explanation: One compound breaks into simpler products (CuCO₃ → CuO + CO₂).

questions.prompt: Which type of reaction is this? “Limestone is heated to make lime and carbon dioxide.”
questions.explanation: Calcium carbonate breaks down when heated (thermal decomposition).

questions.prompt: Which type of reaction is this? “Silver chloride breaks down in light into silver and chlorine.”
questions.explanation: One compound splits into two simpler products (2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂).

questions.prompt: Which type of reaction is this? “Zinc is added to sulphuric acid, giving zinc sulphate and hydrogen.”
questions.explanation: Zinc (more reactive) displaces hydrogen from the acid.

questions.prompt: Which type of reaction is this? “A more reactive metal pushes a less reactive element out of its compound.”
questions.explanation: The more reactive element takes the place of the less reactive one.

questions.prompt: Which type of reaction is this? “Barium chloride reacts with magnesium sulphate to make barium sulphate and magnesium chloride.”
questions.explanation: Two compounds swap partners to make two new compounds.

questions.prompt: Which type of reaction is this? “Two compounds change places to make two new compounds.”
questions.explanation: This is the definition of a double displacement reaction.

questions.prompt: Which type of reaction is this? “Methane burns in oxygen to make carbon dioxide and water.”
questions.explanation: A fuel reacts with oxygen giving heat and light (CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O).

questions.prompt: Which type of reaction is this? “A fuel reacts with oxygen in the air, giving out heat and light.”
questions.explanation: Combustion is burning — the fuel is oxidised.

questions.prompt: Is this endothermic or exothermic? “Photosynthesis.”
questions.explanation: Light energy is taken in to make sugar.

questions.prompt: Is this endothermic or exothermic? “Cooking food.”
questions.explanation: Heat is taken in to change the food.

questions.prompt: Is this endothermic or exothermic? “Melting ice.”
questions.explanation: Heat is taken in to change solid to liquid.

questions.prompt: Is this endothermic or exothermic? “Melting chocolate.”
questions.explanation: Heat is taken in to melt the solid.

questions.prompt: Is this endothermic or exothermic? “Dissolving sugar in water.”
questions.explanation: A little heat is taken in from the surroundings.

questions.prompt: Is this endothermic or exothermic? “Water evaporating from a puddle.”
questions.explanation: Heat is taken in to turn liquid into vapour.

questions.prompt: Is this endothermic or exothermic? “Baking bread.”
questions.explanation: Heat from the oven is taken in.

questions.prompt: Is this endothermic or exothermic? “Sodium carbonate added to vinegar (temperature falls).”
questions.explanation: The mixture gets colder, so heat is taken in.

questions.prompt: Is this endothermic or exothermic? “Burning a fuel (combustion).”
questions.explanation: Heat and light are given out.

questions.prompt: Is this endothermic or exothermic? “Burning toast.”
questions.explanation: Burning gives out heat.

questions.prompt: Is this endothermic or exothermic? “Water freezing into ice.”
questions.explanation: Heat is given out (released at the back of a freezer).

questions.prompt: Is this endothermic or exothermic? “Rusting of iron.”
questions.explanation: Rusting gives out heat, very slowly.

questions.prompt: Is this endothermic or exothermic? “Neutralisation (antacid or toothpaste).”
questions.explanation: Neutralisation gives out heat (a small amount).

questions.prompt: Is this endothermic or exothermic? “Respiration in cells.”
questions.explanation: Energy is released from food inside the cells.
